changes: Actual fix for the chat scroll bug, based on real video evidence this time rather than another blind CSS theory. The recording showed the PAGE BEHIND the chat modal scrolling (Home → Board → back) while the chat's own message list stayed frozen at the same position throughout — textbook scroll-chaining, evidently strong enough that overscroll-behavior:contain alone (already present from a few versions back) wasn't stopping it in the browser it was tested on. Added a touchmove listener on the chat modal that explicitly intercepts any drag NOT targeting the message list and blocks it outright, so a gesture anywhere else in the modal can never be handed off to the page underneath — only the message list itself is ever allowed to scroll. The standard, forceful, JS-level fix for this bug class, used because two rounds of CSS-only attempts already failed or had uncertain effect.

Filtered legacy-format Casino Pot payouts (label like "(2026-09)" with no day suffix, from before the twice-monthly migration) out of the Floor feed. This was genuinely NOT a repeat of the duplicate-payout bug — the countdown card and pot total were both behaving normally, and these entries used the old label format the current system never writes — but stale positive-amount "Casino Pot – Jackpot/Even Split" entries kept surfacing in the "recent activity" feed during quiet periods and getting mistaken for a live repeat, twice now. Reused the existing FLOOR_FEED_EXCLUDE_PATTERN mechanism rather than inventing a new one.

Rolled back part of the previous chat scroll fix, per a follow-up report that it's still fully broken even with .9 confirmed live — two attempts in a row have now failed on this bug. Removed the two riskiest pieces rather than guessing a third theory: the visualViewport-driven inline-style JS (inline styles override every CSS rule including the dvh fallback, and could permanently lock in a wrong height if read even slightly early), and touch-action:pan-y in dashboard.css (unlike overscroll-behavior, which is benign and stays, touch-action can override default scroll-gesture handling outright and is a known cause of scrolling breaking completely on some Android WebViews). Isolating variables before the next attempt rather than piling on more unverified changes — still needs a screen recording and browser identification to actually diagnose properly from here.

Fixed the real cause of a chat scroll bug reported live: Group Chat and Syndy AI chat (shared modal) stopped scrolling entirely, specifically after the on-screen keyboard opened and closed once. That's the signature of vh-based height not reliably recomputing on mobile once the keyboard closes — which is what .syndy-chat-sheet's height:min(88vh,720px) was vulnerable to. Fixed properly this time: dashboard.css now layers in a min(88dvh,720px) variant (dvh tracks the actual visible viewport including keyboard state, unlike plain vh), and a new visualViewport.resize listener explicitly re-asserts the correct pixel height on every real viewport change while the chat's open — the standard robust fix for this exact bug class.

Retroactively logging a change that shipped last turn without a version bump: added overscroll-behavior:contain and touch-action:pan-y to .syndy-chat-body and .profile-modal in dashboard.css, aimed at an earlier report of the same chat window (background page scrolling instead of the message list). That fix targeted the wrong layer of the problem — the real cause was the vh/keyboard issue fixed above — and per the follow-up report actually made things worse, since contain blocked the accidental page-scroll fallback that had been partially masking the underlying bug. Left in place since it's still correct, standard practice on its own merits once the real height bug above is fixed.

Added Casino Pot diagnostics to the Diag tab's Full System Check, per request, so faults surface proactively rather than needing another incident to notice. Four new checks: distribution lock health (flags a lock older than its 10-minute self-heal window — real evidence a run crashed before cleaning up), overdue distribution (the most actionable one — flags any closed period that should have paid out and been deleted but wasn't, meaning real XP is stuck), legacy period-key format (flags any leftover old-style "YYYY-MM" bucket the new twice-monthly logic can't see at all), and weeklyTopupLastRun shape (regression guard for the exact object-instead-of-timestamp mistake the Sept 1 full-reset script made). Also noted plainly why the scheduled function itself can't be pinged directly like the other Netlify functions already on this list (scheduled functions have no public URL) and that a duplicate .mjs/.js situation — which genuinely happened this week — wouldn't be caught by any live check, so that's still worth an occasional manual look in Netlify's Functions tab.

Reversed the pre-launch transition per request: tracking now starts immediately (today, Sept 1) instead of waiting until Sept 16, so the first payment lands 8am AEST Sept 16 rather than Oct 1. Safe to do since balance, lifetime XP, and the pot itself were already fully reset earlier — there was no bad data left to protect against, so the wait was no longer needed. Removed the transition-window code entirely rather than just moving the date, since today's partial 1st–15th window is now just an ordinary (if slightly short) tracked period like any other going forward.

Fixed a real ambiguity in the Casino Pot countdown text. "redistributed 8am AEST on the 1st" during the pre-launch transition window (before Sept 16) read as if it were an imminent date, when it actually meant October 1st — four weeks out. Now spells out the month explicitly during that window only ("first payout 8am AEST 1 October"), computed from the real payout date of the first tracked period rather than hardcoded. Once tracking is live the short "16th"/"1st" wording returns, since at that point the payout is always within ~15 days and genuinely unambiguous.

Fixed a real UI bug on the Casino Pot panel: the "redistributed 8am AEST on the 1st" text under the countdown was leftover from before the twice-monthly change — hardcoded, and wrong for any period that actually pays out on the 16th. Now derived from the period key itself each time the countdown re-renders (ends "-01" → pays the 16th, ends "-16" → pays the 1st), so it's always correct and updates automatically as the date rolls forward — nothing hardcoded.

Casino Pot even-split and jackpot payouts no longer count toward Player Tier, per request. Tier is Player-level lifetime XP + Board Season Score + Tipping points, and the pot payout function now credits balance and logs the payout as always, but deliberately stops adding to lifetime XP — the money's still real and spendable, it just doesn't move tier status. Only genuine game wins, tipping results, and board results affect tier now. Triple-checked the full distribution path end to end while making this change: the shared lock and history idempotency check both still correctly gate every write, the 1st/16th 8am timing is intact, the 75/25 split is intact, and the transition-window guard from the previous update is intact.

Changed the Casino Pot from one monthly distribution to two per month, per request — smaller, more regular payouts instead of one lump sum. Each calendar month is now two periods (1st–15th, 16th–end of month), each paid out 8am AEST/AEDT the day after it closes. Split changed to 75% even-share / 25% jackpot (was 70/30). The switch happened mid-period, so today's partial 1st–15th window was deliberately left untracked and unpaid as a one-off — the first period under the new system is the 16th–30th, paid out 8am October 1st.

Fixed a real bug found while making that change: the eligibility check's "how far back to search this period's play history" window still assumed a full ~32-day month and would have searched into the previous period now that periods are only ~15 days — narrowed to match, so eligibility checks near a period boundary stay accurate.

Changed the Casino Pot split per request: jackpot is now 30% (was 40%), and the remaining 70% (was 60%) splits evenly among everyone eligible — same even-split rule as the previous update, just a different ratio.

Fixed a real bug where the Casino Pot could pay out more than once. The scheduled server job and this app's own "close out last period" check had zero coordination between them — and the app's check re-ran on every new browser session/tab/device rather than just once ever — so multiple copies could all read the same open pot before any of them deleted it, each crediting a full share and drawing its own separate jackpot winner. Both now acquire a shared Firebase lock before touching anything, plus a second check against pot history so the same period can never be paid out twice even if a lock ever went stale.

Split — the last piece of the Blackjack polish arc, now built and verified. Tracks a genuinely second, independent hand per seat rather than reworking the whole model around always-two-hands, the same "parallel track, only populated when actually used" approach single-player Blackjack itself takes for its own split.

New split action on the server, with the same value-match rule single-player uses (a Ten and a King can split together, not just exact rank matches). Hit and Stand both hand off between the two sub-hands within the same seat's own turn before moving on to the next seat. Double is blocked after a split, and a seat can only split once — same simplified rule set single-player already settled on.

Settlement now evaluates each sub-hand independently against the dealer. This was verified with two direct simulations before shipping, not just written and trusted: one confirming a split hand that wins one side and busts the other nets exactly zero, and a second confirming specifically that a split hand landing on 21 pays as a regular win, not a blackjack — both came back correct.

On the table itself: both hands now show side by side with a marker for whichever one is currently active, a Split button that only ever appears when splitting is actually legal, and the results panel breaks a split hand into its own two lines plus the combined total rather than a single outcome word that wouldn't mean anything for two separate hands.

Also fixed a real bug caught by an actual render before shipping, not assumed away: four action buttons at equal width didn't fit the row — Split was genuinely getting clipped at the edge. Switched to a percentage-based width so it wraps into a clean 2x2 grid instead.
